description: Digital graphic of the Punisher skull logo (Marvel comics vigilante emblem) rendered in black with a carbon-fiber-like texture against a dark background, backlit by a red blood-spatter glow that fills the eye sockets. The Punisher skull was widely used as an emblem in Q-related imagery.

Photograph of three people in wildland-firefighter gear (yellow shirts, red helmets, gloves, packs) posing on a wooded hillside and holding a black Antifascist Action flag with the red-and-black twin-flags logo; a chainsaw lies on the ground. Faces are blacked out. A red arrow and circle have been drawn on the image pointing to a red fuel canister on one persons pack, implying arson. This image circulated during the September 2020 West Coast wildfires with the claim that antifa members were setting fires.
flags: Annotation implies the fuel can is evidence of arson — a fuel can is standard wildland firefighting equipment (drip torch fuel); the arson implication is unverified
Individuals are anonymized (faces blacked out) and remain unidentified private individuals
Location and date not shown; September 2020 West Coast wildfire context inferred from circulation

description: Screenshot of a social-media link preview from freightbrokerlive.com showing a 2x4 grid of eight booking/mugshot-style photos of adults, each stamped with the word ARSON in red. The sarcastic headline claims these are the first confirmed photos of Global Warming, implying the 2020 wildfires were caused by arsonists rather than climate conditions. The pictured individuals are not named in the image.
text: ARSON. ARSON. ARSON. ARSON. ARSON. ARSON. ARSON. ARSON. FREIGHTBROKERLIVE.COM. BREAKING: First confirmed photos of Global Warming captured! Wildfire updates
flags: Implied claim that arson, not climate, caused the wildfires is presented as mockery and is unverified as framed

description: Nine-photo collage headlined ANTIFA UNITS TRAINING AND FIGHTING IN SYRIA, credited to XRVision Sentinel AI. Each photo shows masked, armed fighters in militia/camouflage gear posing with antifa (Antifaschistische Aktion two-flag logo), anarchist, red-star, and Kurdish YPG/YPJ-style flags amid Syrian-conflict settings — rubbled buildings, an armored vehicle, desert terrain. The collage claims these are antifa members who fought in Syria, a reference to Western volunteers with Kurdish forces.
text: ANTIFA UNITS TRAINING AND FIGHTING IN SYRIA. ANTIFASCHISTISCHE AKTION. Generated with XRVision Sentinel AI. XRVision. Wearable and Mobile Video Analytics
flags: The headline claim that these are organized antifa units fighting in Syria is the collages assertion; the photos origins and the fighters affiliations are not verifiable from the image
All individuals are masked and unidentified
Location claimed as Syria in the caption; consistent with but not proven by the imagery

description: Six-panel comparison meme equating the 1932-33 German Antifaschistische Aktion with modern antifa. Top row pairs the historical red KPD-era logo, captioned 1933 Paramilitary Wing of The Communist Party of Germany, with the modern red-and-black Antifascist Action logo, captioned 2017 Paramilitary Wing of The Democratic Party of America. Below are two black-and-white photos of 1930s German antifascist rallies with banners, a color photo of masked black-bloc demonstrators posing with antifa flags and sticks, and antifa stickers including Nationalists Not Welcome and Support Your Local Antifa.
text: 1933 Paramilitary Wing of The Communist Party of Germany. 2017 Paramilitary Wing of The Democratic Party of America. ANTIFASCHISTISCHE AKTION. ANTIFASCIST ACTION. NATIONALISTS NOT WELCOME. ANTIFASCIST ACTION. SUPPORT YOUR LOCAL ANTIFA
flags: The captions claim that antifa is the paramilitary wing of the Democratic Party is the memes assertion and is unsubstantiated
Historical framing (Antifaschistische Aktion as a 1933 paramilitary wing) is the memes simplified claim; the group was a KPD campaign founded in 1932
Demonstrators in the modern photo are masked and unidentified
